ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two resonance Lewis structures of nitric acid HNO3, connected in the middle by a double-headed arrow. In each structure, N is located at the center and connected to three O atoms; one of the O atoms is connected to H to form an H–O–N fragment, and the other two O atoms and N interchange in single-bond/double-bond form in the resonance structures. In the figure, no lone-pair electrons are drawn around the N atom. Reasoning: Around N there are three electron domains, namely three N–O bonding regions; a double bond is also counted as one electron domain according to VSEPR. Therefore the local electron-domain geometry of N is trigonal planar. Since the molecular skeleton H–O–N(O)–O of HNO3 is built on this trigonal-planar N center, the HNO3 molecule is planar.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify N as the central atom connected to three O atoms and with no lone pairs on N. Count three electron domains around N. Use VSEPR to assign trigonal planar geometry at nitrogen. Since the molecular skeleton H–O–N(O)–O is built from this trigonal planar N center, conclude that HNO3 molecules are planar.
